answer: A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 18 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The fable detector writes to basalt, and kernel shows every merge. Submissions that land within 102 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 20 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
